nominees.affiliation: Max Planck Institute of Quantum Optics and Ludwig-Maximilians-Universität München, Germany

subfield: Atomic, molecular and optical physics / quantum simulation
motivation: In 1998 Jaksch, Cirac, Zoller and co-workers showed that neutral atoms in laser-made optical lattices realise the Bose-Hubbard model, with parameters tunable by light. In 2002 Bloch and co-workers observed the superfluid-to-Mott-insulator transition exactly as predicted. This turned Feynman's idea of a quantum simulator into a laboratory reality. Cirac and Zoller's theory, from the ion-trap quantum gate to lattice proposals, and Bloch's experiments, including quantum gas microscopy, entanglement measurements and many-body localisation, produced a new way to study strongly correlated matter. Researchers can now prepare, control and image quantum many-body states atom by atom. The combination of bold theory and patient, precise experiment in atomic physics has shaped condensed-matter physics, quantum information and metrology. After more than two decades it is a mature tool used worldwide. It is a discovery of the highest rank that has not yet been recognised.
